# Network and Wi-Fi. Slots: {host} {url} {port} {name} {text}

## Addresses

? my ip address | local ip | what is my ip | ip address | show my ip | ip
Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object { $_.IPAddress -notmatch '^(127|169\.254)\.' } | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, IPAddress, PrefixLength
= Shows the local IPv4 address of each connected adapter.

? public ip | external ip | internet ip | what is my public ip | my ip on the internet
Get-PublicIP
= Asks ipify.org for the public IP address your network uses on the internet (Sensei helper).

? copy my ip to the clipboard | copy ip address
(Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object { $_.IPAddress -notmatch '^(127|169\.254)\.' } | Select-Object -First 1).IPAddress | Set-Clipboard; Get-Clipboard
= Copies your local IP address to the clipboard.

? network configuration | gateway and dns | ip configuration | network settings summary
Get-NetIPConfiguration | Where-Object IPv4DefaultGateway | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, @{n='IPv4';e={$_.IPv4Address.IPAddress}}, @{n='Gateway';e={$_.IPv4DefaultGateway.NextHop}}, @{n='DNS';e={$_.DNSServer.ServerAddresses -join ', '}}
= Shows IP address, router and DNS servers of each connected adapter.

? ipconfig | ipconfig all | full ip configuration
ipconfig /all
= Shows the complete IP configuration of every adapter.

? mac address | physical address
Get-NetAdapter | Select-Object Name, MacAddress, Status
= Shows the MAC address of every network adapter.

? network adapters | network cards | link speed | adapters
Get-NetAdapter | Select-Object Name, InterfaceDescription, Status, LinkSpeed, MacAddress
= Lists network adapters with status, speed and MAC address.

? default gateway | router ip | router address
Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '0.0.0.0/0' | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, NextHop, RouteMetric
= Shows the router (default gateway) address.

? open the router page | router settings | router admin page
Start-Process ("http://" + (Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '0.0.0.0/0' | Sort-Object RouteMetric | Select-Object -First 1).NextHop)
= Opens your router's web page in the browser.

? devices on my network | who is connected to my wifi | other computers on the network | arp table
Get-NetNeighbor -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object { $_.State -in 'Reachable', 'Stale', 'Permanent' -and $_.IPAddress -notmatch '^(224|239|255)\.' -and $_.LinkLayerAddress -notmatch '^(FF-FF|00-00-00-00-00-00)' } | Select-Object IPAddress, LinkLayerAddress, State
= Lists devices your PC has recently talked to on the local network.

## Connectivity

? am I online | is the internet working | internet connection check | am I connected | check internet | check if my internet is working | is my internet down | is the internet down
Test-Connection -TargetName 1.1.1.1 -Count 1 -Quiet
= True when the internet can be reached.

? ping {host} | is {host} reachable | is {host} up | test connection to {host} | check {host}
Test-Connection -TargetName {{host}} -Count 4 | Select-Object Address, Latency, Status
= Sends 4 pings to {host} and shows the response times.

? is {host} down | is {host} working | website status of {host} | check if {host} is online
try { $r = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://{{host}}" -Method Head -TimeoutSec 15 -MaximumRedirection 5; "{{host}} is up (HTTP $($r.StatusCode))" } catch { "{{host}} did not answer: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
= Checks whether the website {host} answers.

? internet speed | speed test | how fast is my internet | test my connection speed | download speed
Test-InternetSpeed
= Downloads 25 MB from Cloudflare and reports Mbps and ping (Sensei helper).

? test port {port} on {host} | is port {port} open on {host} | check port {port} on {host}
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName {{host}} -Port {{port}} | Select-Object ComputerName, RemotePort, TcpTestSucceeded
= Checks whether a TCP connection to {host}:{port} succeeds.

? traceroute {host} | trace route to {host} | tracert {host}
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName {{host}} -TraceRoute | Select-Object -ExpandProperty TraceRoute
= Lists every router hop on the way to {host}.

? dns lookup {host} | resolve {host} | nslookup {host} | ip of {host} | what is the ip of {host}
Resolve-DnsName -Name {{host}} -Type A | Select-Object Name, IPAddress
= Looks up the IP addresses of {host}.

? who owns the domain {host} | whois {host}
Resolve-DnsName -Name {{host}} -Type NS | Select-Object Name, NameHost
= Shows the name servers of {host} (Windows has no whois tool built in).

## Ports

? which process is using port {port} | what is listening on port {port} | port {port} in use | who uses port {port}
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort {{port}} -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, State, OwningProcess, @{n='Process';e={(Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ProcessName}}
= Shows which process owns port {port}. No output means nothing uses it.

? kill the process on port {port} | free port {port} | stop whatever uses port {port}
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort {{port}} -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty OwningProcess -Unique | Where-Object { $_ -gt 4 } | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_ -Force -PassThru } | Select-Object Name, Id
= Ends the process that holds port {port}.

? open ports | listening ports | which ports are open on my pc
Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Sort-Object LocalPort | Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess, @{n='Process';e={(Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ProcessName}}
= Lists every TCP port your PC listens on and the program behind it.

? active connections | what is connected to the internet | established connections | which programs use the internet
Get-NetTCPConnection -State Established | Where-Object RemoteAddress -notmatch '^(127\.|::1)' | Select-Object RemoteAddress, RemotePort, @{n='Process';e={(Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ProcessName}} | Sort-Object Process
= Lists open internet connections and which program made them.

? open port {port} in the firewall | allow port {port} | firewall rule for port {port}
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Sensei - allow TCP {{port}}" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort {{port}} -Action Allow | Select-Object DisplayName, Enabled
= Allows incoming TCP connections on port {port}.
! admin

? close port {port} in the firewall | remove the firewall rule for port {port}
Remove-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Sensei - allow TCP {{port}}"; 'Rule removed.'
= Removes the rule Sensei made for port {port}.
! admin

## DNS

? dns servers | which dns am I using
Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object ServerAddresses | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, ServerAddresses
= Lists the DNS servers each adapter uses.

? flush dns | clear dns cache | reset dns cache
Clear-DnsClientCache; 'DNS cache cleared.'
= Empties the DNS cache.

? use cloudflare dns | set dns to 1.1.1.1 | change dns to cloudflare
Get-NetAdapter -Physical | Where-Object Status -eq 'Up' | ForEach-Object { Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex $_.ifIndex -ServerAddresses 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1 }; Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object ServerAddresses
= Sets Cloudflare DNS (1.1.1.1) on connected adapters.
! admin

? use google dns | set dns to 8.8.8.8 | change dns to google
Get-NetAdapter -Physical | Where-Object Status -eq 'Up' | ForEach-Object { Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex $_.ifIndex -ServerAddresses 8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4 }; Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object ServerAddresses
= Sets Google DNS (8.8.8.8) on connected adapters.
! admin

? reset dns to automatic | automatic dns | use router dns
Get-NetAdapter -Physical | ForEach-Object { Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex $_.ifIndex -ResetServerAddresses }; Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object ServerAddresses
= Goes back to the DNS servers your router hands out.
! admin

? hosts file | show the hosts file
Get-Content "$env:windir\System32\drivers\etc\hosts"
= Prints the hosts file.

? edit the hosts file | change hosts file
Start-Process notepad -ArgumentList "$env:windir\System32\drivers\etc\hosts" -Verb RunAs
= Opens the hosts file in Notepad as administrator.

? block {host} | block the website {host}
Add-Content -Path "$env:windir\System32\drivers\etc\hosts" -Value "`n0.0.0.0 {{host}}`n0.0.0.0 www.{{host}}"; Clear-DnsClientCache; 'Blocked {{host}} in the hosts file.'
= Blocks {host} on this PC through the hosts file.
! admin

## Wi-Fi

? saved wifi networks | wifi profiles | networks I connected to before | known wifi networks
netsh wlan show profiles
= Lists the Wi-Fi networks saved on this PC.

? wifi password | show my wifi password | password of my wifi | what is my wifi password | current wifi password
Get-WifiPassword
= Shows the password of the Wi-Fi you are connected to (Sensei helper).

? wifi password of {name} | password for the wifi {text} | show the password of {name}
Get-WifiPassword -Name "{{name}}"
= Shows the saved password of the Wi-Fi network {name}.

? available wifi networks | wifi networks nearby | scan for wifi | which wifi can I connect to
netsh wlan show networks mode=bssid
= Lists Wi-Fi networks in range with signal strength.

? current wifi | wifi signal strength | which wifi am I connected to | wifi speed | wifi status | is wifi on | is wifi connected | am I on wifi
netsh wlan show interfaces
= Shows the connected network, signal strength and speed.

? connect to wifi {name} | join the network {name}
netsh wlan connect name="{{name}}"
= Connects to the saved Wi-Fi network {name}.

? connect to wifi {text} | connect to {text} wifi | join wifi {text}
netsh wlan connect name="{{text}}"
= Connects to the saved Wi-Fi network {text}.

? disconnect wifi | disconnect from wifi | leave the wifi network
netsh wlan disconnect
= Disconnects from the current Wi-Fi network (Wi-Fi stays on).

? turn off wifi | wifi off | disable wifi | switch off wifi
Set-WifiState -Off
= Turns the Wi-Fi adapter off (Sensei helper).
! admin

? turn on wifi | wifi on | enable wifi | switch on wifi
Set-WifiState -On
= Turns the Wi-Fi adapter on (Sensei helper).
! admin

? forget wifi {name} | delete the saved wifi {name} | remove wifi network {name}
netsh wlan delete profile name="{{name}}"
= Deletes the saved Wi-Fi network {name} and its password.

? wifi report | wifi problems history
netsh wlan show wlanreport
= Creates an HTML report of Wi-Fi sessions and errors from the last 3 days.
! admin

? wifi settings | open wifi settings
Start-Process "ms-settings:network-wifi"
= Opens Wi-Fi settings.

? airplane mode | flight mode
Start-Process "ms-settings:network-airplanemode"
= Opens Airplane mode settings (Windows has no command to switch it directly).

? mobile hotspot | share my internet | turn on hotspot
Start-Process "ms-settings:network-mobilehotspot"
= Opens Mobile hotspot settings.

## Other

? network profile | is my network public or private
Get-NetConnectionProfile | Select-Object Name, InterfaceAlias, NetworkCategory, IPv4Connectivity
= Shows whether each network is Public or Private.

? set the network to private | make network private | change network to private
Get-NetConnectionProfile | Set-NetConnectionProfile -NetworkCategory Private; Get-NetConnectionProfile | Select-Object Name, NetworkCategory
= Marks the current network as Private (allows sharing and discovery).
! admin

? set the network to public | make network public
Get-NetConnectionProfile | Set-NetConnectionProfile -NetworkCategory Public; Get-NetConnectionProfile | Select-Object Name, NetworkCategory
= Marks the current network as Public (safer on cafe/hotel Wi-Fi).
! admin

? shared folders | smb shares | what do I share on the network
Get-SmbShare | Select-Object Name, Path, Description
= Lists folders this PC shares on the network.

? vpn connections | vpn status | am I on vpn
Get-VpnConnection -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, ServerAddress, ConnectionStatus; Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object { $_.InterfaceDescription -match 'VPN|TAP|WireGuard|Tailscale|NordLynx' } | Select-Object Name, InterfaceDescription, Status
= Shows Windows VPN connections and VPN adapters (NordVPN, Tailscale ...) with their status.

? proxy settings | am I using a proxy
netsh winhttp show proxy; Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings' | Select-Object ProxyEnable, ProxyServer
= Shows the system and user proxy settings.

? reset network | fix internet problems | winsock reset | network reset
netsh winsock reset; netsh int ip reset; ipconfig /flushdns
= Resets the Windows network stack. Restart the PC afterwards.
! admin

? renew ip | get a new ip address | release and renew
ipconfig /release; ipconfig /renew
= Asks the router for a fresh IP address (the connection drops for a moment).

? enable remote desktop | turn on remote desktop | allow remote connections | rdp
Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption; Start-Process "ms-settings:remotedesktop"
= Opens Remote Desktop settings. Windows Home editions cannot accept Remote Desktop connections (Pro can); use Quick Assist or another remote tool instead.

? remote help | quick assist | let someone help me remotely
Start-Process "ms-quick-assist:"
= Opens Quick Assist, Windows' built-in remote help.

? data used by apps | network usage per app
Start-Process "ms-settings:datausage"
= Opens Data usage settings, which list how much data each app used.
